what_its_for: Lenvatinib is a cancer medicine used to treat certain types of thyroid cancer, kidney cancer, liver cancer (hepatocellular carcinoma), and a type of uterine cancer called endometrial carcinoma. It works by blocking signals that help cancer cells grow and by cutting off the blood supply that tumors need to survive.
how_to_take: Swallow the capsules whole with or without food at the same time every day. Do not open, crush, or chew the capsules. If you cannot swallow capsules, you may dissolve them in a small amount of water or apple juice — ask your pharmacist or doctor how to do this correctly. Wash your hands after handling the capsules.
dosing: Your doctor will prescribe the dose that is right for your specific cancer type and your body. Common doses range from 8 mg to 24 mg taken once daily, but your dose may be adjusted based on how well you tolerate the medicine and how well it is working. Always take exactly the dose your doctor prescribes — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and it has been LESS than 12 hours since your scheduled time, take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it has been MORE than 12 hours, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular time the next day. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store lenvatinib capsules at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep the capsules in their original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep away from heat, moisture, and light. Keep out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of any leftover capsules.
what_to_avoid: Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice, as they may affect how your body processes this medicine. Avoid becoming pregnant while taking lenvatinib, as it can cause serious harm or death to an unborn baby. Use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 30 days after your last dose. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine. Avoid taking herbal supplements like St. John's Wort without first asking your doctor. Tell your doctor about ALL other medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, as lenvatinib can interact with many drugs including blood thinners, certain antibiotics, and antifungal medicines.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: very high blood pressure or a sudden severe headache; chest pain, shortness of breath, or a fast or irregular heartbeat; signs of a stroke such as sudden numbness, weakness, confusion, vision changes, or difficulty speaking; severe stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea; blood in your stool or very dark tarry stools; coughing up blood; unusual bleeding or bruising; painful or swollen hands and feet (hand-foot syndrome); signs of a hole or tear in your stomach or bowel such as severe abdominal pain and fever; swelling in your legs or ankles; changes in urination or signs of kidney problems; extreme tiredness or yellowing of your skin or eyes (signs of liver problems); or any wound that is not healing properly.
when_it_works: Lenvatinib starts working at the cellular level right away, but it may take several weeks to months before you or your doctor notice changes in your tumor size or symptoms. Your doctor will schedule regular blood tests, imaging scans, and check-ups to monitor how well the medicine is working. Do not stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor, even if you feel well.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Do not use lenvatinib if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. Use reliable birth control during treatment and for at least 30 days after stopping. Children: Lenvatinib is not approved for use in children under 18 years of age for most indications. Older adults (65 and older): You can take lenvatinib, but your doctor will monitor you closely as side effects such as high blood pressure and fatigue may be more common. Kidney or liver problems: If you have moderate or severe liver or kidney disease, your doctor may start you on a lower dose and will monitor you more closely. Always tell your healthcare team about all your medical conditions before starting this medicine.
